input.summary:
parts/room-7.mjs (room: P3 front room) now builds clean: the duplicate lit smoker at 40,3,12 is dropped from the room layer, since Hearths already places it facing east.
Last make.sh run: P3 front room reports 7 placed, 0 refused, 0 off-palette; build.nbt written.
Only parts/room-7.mjs was edited.
left: Same refusal in other room parts, out of scope here: room: P0 front room (7,3,12 smoker) and room: P1 east flat (19,3,12 smoker) each re-place a smoker the Hearths part already built. Each needs the same one-line removal in its own module.
Walkability and fit were not re-run after the edit (mcd room / mcd fit on rooms.json). Dropping S leaves 40,3,12 as the Hearths smoker only; the room's furniture is otherwise unchanged.

waste.what: Worked out which layer row maps to which z and which cell collides with the stove placed by Hearths, by reading the layers() grid by hand against the report's refusedAt coordinates.
waste.cost: 2 reads of the part and report files plus one grep of hearths.mjs to confirm the stove's position and facing; about 3 tool calls.
waste.tool: make.sh / runParts report could print, for each refused write, the earlier part and call that placed the cell (e.g. 'hearths.mjs:17 stove(40,3,12,east)') and the layer row and column that produced it, so the fix is a lookup, not a reconstruction.

waste.what: Had to decide by hand that the room's smoker duplicated the Hearths stove and that dropping it was right, with no tool flagging the duplicate by block id and facing.
waste.cost: One grep of hearths.mjs and a judgment call; no retries.
waste.tool: A layers() dry-run or a 'would be refused' pre-check (for example mcd plan with the earlier parts' cells marked 'o' as the room already shows) would flag the S cell before make.sh runs. The room designer's plan output already marks existing cells 'o', so a pre-check of the Hearths stove would have shown the collision at the authoring step.
